title: Guitarron (Mexican bass guitar)
summary: The guitarron is the big bass guitar of Mexican folk bands. It has a huge round belly, a short wide neck and six thick strings that are plucked in pairs, an octave apart, for a deep, ringing pulse. It lays the foundation under fiddles, trumpets and smaller guitars.
howToPlay: Six strings run down the wide neck, the lowest on the left. Each lane marks the place where a note is played.
A bead slides down the string to its place. Pluck the lane as the bead lands.
The wide lane over the strings is a chord: tap it to sound the strings together.
Try the bass walk first, then the octave leaps, then the slow march.
rules: The notes come from a seven-note scale starting on A, from low A up to the top string.
Every phrase is played through twice.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
The octave leaps count two beats to the bar; the others count four.
heritageNote: The guitarron grew out of older bass guitars of the Spanish world and is now part of Mexican folk bands. Makers shape its deep, bulging belly by hand, so every instrument has its own deep voice.
